items.t: FBI arrests OpenAI employee accused of planting hidden recording device in conference room
items.d: It's not clear exactly for what purpose the recording device was used, but FBI director Kash Patel said the scheme was to "capture sensitive communications about the company’s super intelligence technology."
items.fullText: OpenAI said it has alerted the FBI after discovering that an employee allegedly planted a hidden recording device in one of the AI maker’s office executive conference rooms. The employee, named by federal prosecutors as Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was fired and arrested on October 9, about a week after OpenAI discovered the surveillance device. The company said in a post on X that it used its internal AI models to understand the “sophisticated” device. OpenAI told TechCrunch that the device contained “advanced encryption, audio monitoring capabilities, and a mechanism for transferring data designed to evade monitoring,” though it is unclear to what degree this device is technically distinct from other recording devices. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data,” said OpenAI in its post on X. OpenAI’s spokesperson, Nate Evans, confirmed that the employee started with the AI model maker in July 2025 and worked on the product team. Prosecutors with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of California said Alfozan was charged with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications — effectively accusing him of covertly recording people’s voice audio without their permission. Prosecutors said OpenAI caught the device after it was inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in OpenAI’s San Francisco office. Per the prosecutors, Alfozan was caught looking behind the television where the recording device was placed, and where OpenAI had placed a camera that allegedly caught the employee. items.t: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
items.d: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
items.fullText: A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July. Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device. These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations and records showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components. The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited. The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services. In its lawsuit, Apple accused OpenAI of a pattern of theft, which includes direct complaints about former employees using Apple laptops to download confidential material and files that contained information about unannounced technologies, features, and products, including technical specifications, engineering presentations, and proprietary project data. Apple also said that former Apple employees at OpenAI coached others considering leaving Apple for OpenAI on what information to bring to their interviews, among other allegations. U.S. District Judge Edward Davila didn’t greenlight all of Apple’s requests for expedited access to OpenAI documents and messages relevant to the case. items.t: Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police
items.d: The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.”
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Matt Rourke / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 13, 2026, 2:24 PM EDT By David K. Li Artificial intelligence research company Anthropic said one of its models generated a bogus tip about an unsolved murder and submitted it to Philadelphia police, warning that the incident raises concerns about high-tech “behaviors” that “could do far more harm as models become more powerful.” The AI model reached out to PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com , part of the police department, on July 18 and made a “false homicide tip,” Philadelphia police said Tuesday in a statement. The agency flagged the tip as spam, and it was never forwarded to investigators, police said. The police department emphasized that all tips have to go through human vetting before they ever get to a detective’s desk. “The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” it said. “Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess — not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence,” the statement said. “An automated submission does not bypass that process.” Anthropic said in a statement that its Claude Haiku 4.5 “had been tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages.” And in a run on July 18, Claude “landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide” and came to a page that “contained a tip form run by a police department,” Anthropic said. items.t: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.d: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
items.fullText: If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable. “Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence , told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.” Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it. “Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said. Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon , October 13. Howie Sun, CEO, Laplace Intelligence. Image Credits: Laplace Intelligence Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. In 2023, he and Liu — his then-PhD adviser — published a paper on the subject that made it onto the cover of the top scientific journal Nature. That’s when the calls started coming in from autonomous vehicle companies interested in implementing their ideas. “I realized that I wanted to build this and take it from purely academic research into a product that’s useful in the real world,” Sun said. items.fullText: AI·SW AI [라이징 2026] 헬러마크 워크데이 CAIO “HR·IT 업무, AI 에이전트 하나로 해결” 발행일 : 2026-10-13 22:00 지면 : 2026-10-14 11면 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 조엘 헬러마크 워크데이 최고AI책임자(CAIO)가 12일(현지시간) 미국 라스베이거스 베네시안 컨벤션센터에서 열린 '라이징 2026'에서 아시아태평양 기자단과 인터뷰하고 있다. ⓒ박종진기자 워크데이가 인사관리(HR)·정보기술(IT) 업무를 자연어 입력 한 번에 해결하는 인공지능(AI) 에이전트 '사나 컨시어지(Sana Concierge)'를 출시한다. 조엘 헬러마크 워크데이 최고AI책임자(CAIO)는 12일(현지시간) 미국 라스베이거스 베네시안 컨벤션센터에서 열린 '라이징 2026' 아시아태평양 기자단 그룹인터뷰에서 “기업 내 직원 인사 업무와 IT 시스템 관리에 특화된, 실시간 접근이 가능한 단일 인터페이스를 제공할 것”이라며 이같이 말했다. 사나 컨시어지는 임직원 입·퇴사 절차와 휴가·급여 문의, 비밀번호 재설정, 애플리케이션 접근 권한 등 인사와 IT 관련 업무 전반을 에이전틱 AI 기반 자체 지원한다. 예를 들어 직원이 육아휴직 기간과 급여 지급 방식 등을 질문하면 관련 정책과 개인 정보를 확인하고, HR·급여 담당 부서·관리자의 승인 절차를 조율하는 방식이다. 사람의 판단이 필요한 경우에는 담당자에 처리 이력과 관련 정보, 후속 조치 권고 사항을 전달해 투명성을 높인다. 기업 정책과 접근 권한에 따라 허용된 범위에서 명령을 직접 실행하고 문제를 해결하도록 설계된 게 강점이다. 기업별 사나 컨시어지 이용이 거듭되면 HR과 IT 관련 빈번한 요청을 학습·분석, 기업 맞춤형 업무 자동화를 실현하는 핵심 데이터로 활용될 예정이다. 사나 컨시어지는 내년 1월 공식 출시될 예정으로, 일부 고객사 대상 베타 버전이 제공되고 있다. 기업들은 고객 대면 업무와 내부 운영에 도입, 직원 업무와 서비스 효율 등 생산성이 개선될 것으로 기대한다. 워크데이는 AI 업무 자율성을 높임과 동시에 기업 통제를 유지하는 데 중점을 두고 있다. 고객사와 파트너가 개발한 에이전트에도 동일하게 적용된다. 특히 기업 업무에 활용되는 복수의 AI 에이전트 조율을 지원하는 워크데이 '사나'는 AI 추론 능력과 자사 결정론적 비즈니스 프로세스를 결합해 조직별 정책·권한과 승인 절차 안에서 작동한다. 무조건적으로 AI에 의존하는 게 아닌 동일한 조건과 입력이 주어지면 사전에 정의된 업무 규칙에 따라 일관되고 예측 가능한 결과를 도출하는 방식을 병행 활용한다. 자연어 기반 지시를 하면서도 기업 정책에 어긋나지 않는 결과를 얻을 수 있도록 설계한 것이다. 헬러마크 CAIO는 “워크데이 AI 핵심은 추론 모델과 결정론적 가드레일 결합에 있다”며 “IT 업무 프로세스가 계획부터 승인까지 실행되는 방식이 정해진 결정론적 단계라면 어떤 워크플로우를 호출하고 어떻게 순서를 정할지 파악하는 것은 확률적 추론”이라고 설명했다. 이어 “워크데이 상에서 실행되는 AI가 원칙에서 벗어나지 않게 확실히 제어할 수 있는 방법”이라며 “기업에 도움이 되지 않을 비정상적인 에이전트가 생성되지 않도록 제어·감독하는 것도 핵심 역량”이라고 덧붙였다. 라스베이거스= 박종진 기자 truth@etnews.com 관련 기사 워크데이, 2분기 매출 3.6조원…“AI가 신규 계약 견인” 재정비 마친 워크데이, AI·파트너 전략 내세워 한국 공략 박차 [라이징 2026] 워크데이, 앤트로픽·일레븐랩스와 협업…“파트너십 지속 확대” 사나 사나 컨시어지 워크데이 인공지능 인공지능에이전트 AI CAIO

AI 반도체주 팔아치운 투자자에 탄 CEO "도박꾼" 빗대며 비판 자사 칩 경쟁우위 강조하려 한듯 “많은 투자자가 자신이 무엇에 투자하는지 전혀 모릅니다. 높은 기대를 품지만 결국에는 카지노에 온 것과 다름없다는 걸 깨닫게 됩니다.” 혹 탄 브로드컴 최고경영자(CEO·사진)가 12일(현지시간) 싱가포르에서 열린 포럼에서 한 이 발언이 반도체주 급락의 계기가 됐다. 인공지능(AI) 투자자들이 도박을 벌이고 있다는 의미로 해석되면서 이날 브로드컴(-1.88%) 엔비디아(-1.29%) Arm(-4.15%) 등을 포함한 필라델피아반도체지수는 전날보다 2.67% 떨어졌다. AI 칩 공급사인 브로드컴이 스스로 시장에 찬물을 끼얹은 셈이다. AI 열풍의 한가운데 있는 그가 자충수를 둔 것으로 보이지만, 오히려 AI의 장기적 가치를 강조한 것이란 분석이 나온다. 블룸버그통신에 따르면 탄 CEO의 발언은 최근 오픈AI 매출에 실망한 투자자를 겨냥한 것이다. 최근 오픈AI의 연환산 매출이 시장 예상치(700억달러)보다 적은 500억달러라는 파이낸셜타임스(FT) 보도에 AI 반도체주를 팔아치운 투자자를 단기 실적에 연연하는 ‘도박꾼’에 빗댄 것이다. 탄 CEO는 “오픈AI가 연환산 매출 500억달러를 거둔 것은 스타트업으로서는 나쁘지 않다”고 평가하며 “오픈AI 같은 첨단 모델 개발사가 향후 소프트웨어 기업을 대체하면서 더 많은 가치를 가져갈 것”이라고 내다봤다. 그는 이어 “이들 첨단 모델 개발사는 약 1000억달러를 지출해 1200억달러 매출을 거두지만, 개방형 모델 진영은 비슷한 1000억달러를 쓰고도 매출이 300억달러에 불과하다”고 강조했다. 이런 발언에 대해 경쟁사인 엔비디아를 견제하고 자사 맞춤형 반도체의 경쟁 우위를 강조하기 위한 것이란 해석이 제기된다. 탄 CEO가 높게 평가한 오픈AI, 앤트로픽, 구글은 브로드컴의 맞춤형 반도체를 쓰거나 개발하고 있다. 반면 엔비디아는 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 시장을 확대하기 위해 탄 CEO가 깎아내린 개방형 모델 생태계를 지원하고 있다. 그는 “특정 AI 작업에서는 800W 전력을 쓰는 맞춤형 칩이 1.4㎾를 쓰는 범용 GPU보다 뛰어난 성능을 낼 수 있다”고 주장했다. 최적화된 자사 칩으로 비용 경쟁력을 확보할 수 있다는 논리다. 탄 CEO는 “AI 생태계의 최대 병목은 메모리가 아니라 자본”이라고도 했다. 자금 부족론은 브로드컴의 금융 전략과 맞물린다. 브로드컴은 블랙스톤, 아폴로 등 금융회사와 협력해 앤트로픽의 AI 칩 확보를 위한 600억달러 구조화 금융 패키지를 주도했다. 오픈AI용 칩을 위한 500억달러 이상의 자금 조달도 추진하고 있다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김인엽 특파원 한국경제신문 실리콘밸리 김인엽 특파원입니다. 정치부, 국제부를 거쳐 테크앤사이언스부에 있습니다. 현재 실리콘밸리 빅테크와 스타트업, 캘리포니아에서 일어나는 흥미로운 일들을 취재하고 있습니다. October 12, 2026 by Nat Ives 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork. The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA’s Investments in France NVIDIA has been investing in France’s startup ecosystem, having previously invested in leading technology companies including Alice&Bob, Gradium and Scintil Photonics . Across all of Europe, NVIDIA has committed nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Doctolib, Entalpic , Genesis AI and Pigment . These startups are innovating to solve challenges across healthcare, materials discovery, physical AI and business planning. Doctolib , a European healthcare technology company, builds agents that free up healthcare professionals to deliver better care, while providing patients with a digital health companion that improves access to care and supports more preventive, continuous medicine. Entalpic , a Paris-based startup, accelerates the engineering of advanced materials at the atomic scale, with particular expertise in surfaces and interfaces for semiconductor manufacturing and next-generation electronics. Genesis AI is a global robotics company developing general-purpose robots with frontier intelligence and capabilities through its foundation models, data collection systems, simulation infrastructure and robot hardware. October 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Humanoid-Warehouse.mp4 Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics ( ovphysx ), scene updates ( ovstage ), rendering ( ovrtx ) and the user interface ( ovui ). items.fullText: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents RTX Spark preorders open today alongside a preview of NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows, the first deskside AI supercomputer built for the Windows enterprise desktop. October 7, 2026 by Gerardo Delgado 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At a Microsoft event in San Francisco on Wednesday, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined how NVIDIA and Microsoft are co-engineering hardware and software for AI agents to run on Windows PCs. NVIDIA was founded because of Windows, Huang said. Now AI agents are coming to Windows. “If you look at the entire journey of our company, Windows was at the core of it,” Huang said, tracing back NVIDIA’s support for Windows and Microsoft over several decades. “If not for Windows there would be no GeForce.” Huang connected that history — and his long-term vision — to the agentic era Wednesday during a fireside chat with Nadella hosted by Sriram Krishnan, a former senior White House policy advisor on AI at the Windows AI and Surface event, held at Dogpatch Studios in San Francisco. “The thing that I really give Jensen all the credit for, quite frankly, is that consistency of vision of what this can be—not today, not tomorrow, but as a secular trend,” Nadella said. “And that’s what brings us to this moment.” “The personal computer is the ultimate tool, it’s my ultimate tool, and for a whole generation of people, it’s our ultimate tool,” Huang said. “What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer? It is now your personal assistant.” The event opened with Nadella before Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president of Windows and Devices at Microsoft, walked through the Windows updates designed for the agentic era.
